newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala says phone company up for bids by April.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala says phone company up for bids by April.

text.p: The state-owned Guatemalan Telecommunications Company (Guatel) will be on the auction block by April, the general manager of the company said on Sunday.
"We will be inviting bidders in April," Guatel general manager told reporters at a news conference.
Guzman said four investment banks -- C.S. First Boston, Lehman Brothers, Salomon Brothers and J.P. Morgan -- have presented proposals to be the lead manager on the sale of Guatel.
One of those will be chosen by the end of February, Guzman said.
The new owners of Guatel will not enjoy a telecommunications monopoly as the state-owned company has for most of its existence.
The government plans to finance 10 percent of its 1997 budget with the privatization of Guatel and other state-owned industries.
The Guatemalan Congress passed a new telecommunications law in October, opening up the industry to international competition for both local and long-distance telephone service.

Guatel on Saturday substantially raised rates for local calls and significantly lowered rates for international calls. The change in rates is meant to make Guatel competitive when other phone companies enter the market.

Guatel, largely through its income from international calls, is one of the government's biggest cash cows, but it does not have enough capital to make the improvements needed to keep up with the demand for new service.

Guatemala has four telephone lines for every 100 people. A million requests for lines are backlogged at Guatel. In Guatemala City alone, 425,000 requests for lines are waiting to be filled. More than 100,000 homes and businesses have paid for new lines, up to 18 months ago, that have not yet been installed.
